detail.body:
[Feat] [Intel] disaggregation: Support XPU for staging-buffer KV transfer

## Dependencies

- **#43299**, "[PD] Fix the early-send wait event on non-CUDA devices and in nixl". Merge it first.
  - Without it, `maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` in `disaggregation/prefill.py` calls `torch.cuda.Event()` when a request hits the prefill prefix cache. On XPU that raises `Tried to instantiate dummy base class Event` and kills the prefill scheduler.
  - The new test's `test_concurrent_matches_serial_with_staging` sends requests that share a prefix, so it hits that path. Until #43299 merges, that test fails, and the fixture then aborts the rest of the file.

## Motivation

Heterogeneous-TP P/D uses the staging buffer to regroup KV between prefill and decode, but the staging path hardcodes CUDA, so it does not run on Intel XPU.

## Modifications

- **Device-neutral staging.** The staging-buffer KV transfer path uses `torch.get_device_module` instead of hardcoded `torch.cuda` calls.
  - On CUDA and ROCm these resolve to the same `torch.cuda` calls, and every behaviour change is gated to XPU.
  - Where the old code could only crash off CUDA, such as a hardcoded `"cuda:{gpu_id}"` device string, the device-neutral call is kept.
  - Staging supports CUDA and XPU; any other device fails at startup with a clear error.
- **Breaking change for out-of-tree backends.** `init_staging_buffers`, `init_staging_allocator` and `init_dcp_pack_buffers` take a required keyword-only `device_type`. The `"cuda"` default was dropped, so no backend can silently allocate staging on CUDA.
- **Pointer tables.** The staging Triton kernels build their per-layer pointer tables with `make_ptr_table` (#35051) instead of `torch.tensor(..., dtype=torch.int64)`, which rejects XPU USM addresses with bit 63 set.
  - XPU therefore takes the Triton gather/scatter path by default, as CUDA does. `SGLANG_STAGING_USE_TORCH=1` still selects the torch fallback.
  - On CUDA the table holds the same int64 values.
- **DCP pack.** The DCP pack kernel still packs its pointers as int64 and has no torch fallback, so off CUDA `init_dcp_pack_buffers` returns no buffers and DCP transfers fall back to per-token RDMA.
- **Decode scatter ordering.** On XPU, the decode-side scatter waits on an event recorded on `schedule_stream` when the room is registered, right after pre-alloc writes its `req_to_token` row. Waiting on the stream itself would also queue each scatter behind any forward running there, losing overlap.
- Adds `create_device_event` to `srt/utils/common.py`.
- **Fix (XPU only): NIXL staging-buffer reuse race** (second commit). When decode TP is larger than prefill attn TP, the NIXL prefill worker gathers each decode rank's head slice into the same staging buffer and posts an asynchronous WRITE, but waited on the handles only after looping over the ranks. The next rank's gather could overwrite the source of a write still in flight, so decode received a mix of two ranks' heads. On XPU, the worker now waits on each staging write before the next gather; the handle still joins the batch, so the batch-level wait keeps handling failures. The wait is gated to XPU, where the corruption was observed; other devices keep their current behaviour. Mooncake writes synchronously and is unaffected.
- **Tests.**
  - New `test/registered/xpu/test_disaggregation_staging_xpu.py` on `nightly-xpu-kernel-main-4-gpu` runs staging with prefill TP 1 and decode TP 2 on Mooncake (TENT over TCP). It skips when `mooncake.engine` is not installed.
  - The test passes no RDMA devices. In CI the fixture otherwise gives both servers its CUDA-runner default NICs (`mlx5_roce*`), which Mooncake rejects on the XPU runners, which have no RDMA NIC.
  - Decode keeps the default `host_pool` retraction backup, which #32503 enabled on XPU.
  - The decode server runs with `TORCHINDUCTOR_USE_STATIC_CUDA_LAUNCHER=0`. On torch 2.13.0+xpu and 2.14.0+xpu, inductor's static Triton launcher segfaults in `load_kernel` on the compiled vocab-parallel embedding mask, which only runs at TP > 1. Likely pytorch/pytorch#199511; drop the override once the XPU torch pin includes it.
  - New manual `test/manual/kv_transfer/test_disaggregation_staging_nixl_xpu.py` is the NIXL variant. It skips when `nixl` is not installed and sets `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n`; with the memtype cache on, UCX classifies XPU memory as host and NIXL fails to register the KV cache.
  - `test_dcp_pack.py` and `test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py` cover the keyword-only `device_type` and the pointer-table change.
- **Docs.**
  - `pd_disaggregation.mdx` notes that the staging buffer runs on Intel XPU (tested prefill TP 1, decode TP 2 on Mooncake, which needs a TENT build with XPU support).
  - The XPU page's DCP section notes that P/D with DCP on XPU skips the DCP pack fast path.
## Accuracy Tests

**Unit tests (CPU, no accelerator required).** The new tests run under `register_cpu_ci` with stubs and mocks:
- `test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py` (`TestMooncakeStagingDeviceType`): prefill staging buffers and the decode staging allocator receive the runtime device instead of an implicit `"cuda"`. These cover device selection only, not an end-to-end Mooncake staging transfer.
- `test_dcp_pack.py` (`TestInitDcpPackBuffers`): a non-Triton device gets no DCP pack buffers and never registers memory; CUDA buffers use the bare device type and `gpu_id`.
- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/`: 695 passed, 14 skipped.

**XPU end to end.**
- `test/registered/xpu/test_disaggregation_staging_xpu.py` runs prefill TP 1 and decode TP 2, so KV goes through the staging path, on Mooncake (`nightly-xpu-kernel-main-4-gpu`). Mooncake's XPU support lives in its TENT engine, so the test sets `MC_USE_TENT=1` and `MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL=tcp` and needs no RDMA NIC. It skips when `mooncake.engine` is not importable, so the nightly stays green on an image without Mooncake. Its four cases:
  - a single completion through the staging path (prefill and decode both allocate their staging buffers, including the XPU pointer format);
  - deterministic output;
  - concurrent requests matching the serial output;
  - multi-chunk long-sequence generation.
- The concurrent-vs-serial case matters most. It runs with overlap scheduling and a radix-cache prefix hit, and compares against the serial answers at temperature 0, so KV corruption shows up as a token mismatch. It needs #43299. It is also the case that exposed the NIXL staging race fixed here.
- The staging test lives under the `xpu` vendor tree because the registered-test layout rejects new paths outside `<kind>/<subsystem>`, while vendor directories are exempt.
- The NIXL variant is the manual test `test/manual/kv_transfer/test_disaggregation_staging_nixl_xpu.py`. It mirrors the registered scenarios and skips when `nixl` is not installed.
- The staging decode server (TP 2) runs with `TORCHINDUCTOR_USE_STATIC_CUDA_LAUNCHER=0`. On torch 2.13.0+xpu and 2.14.0+xpu, inductor's static Triton launcher segfaults in `load_kernel` on the compiled vocab-parallel embedding mask (`vocab_parallel_embedding._embed_local_shard`), which only runs at TP > 1. Turning off only the static launcher keeps torch.compile on, unlike `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1`. Likely pytorch/pytorch#199511; the override can go once the XPU torch pin includes the fix.

Results on Intel Arc Pro B60, cards 4 to 6, torch 2.14.0+xpu:

| Test | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_dcp_pack.py`, `test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py` (CPU) | this PR | 31 passed |
| `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=4,5,6 python3 -m pytest -v test/registered/xpu/test_disaggregation_staging_xpu.py` | this PR + #43299 | 4/4 passed, 77 s; the Mooncake concurrent case also passed 4 of 4 separate runs |
| same | this PR without #43299 | 2 passed, then `test_concurrent_matches_serial_with_staging` crashed prefill on `torch.cuda.Event()` and the fixture aborted the file |
| same, with `TORCHINDUCTOR_USE_STATIC_CUDA_LAUNCHER=0` removed | this PR + #43299 | The TP-2 decode server segfaults in `static_triton_launcher` `load_kernel` from `vocab_parallel_embedding._embed_local_shard`, so the override is still needed |
| same, with `mooncake` made unimportable | this PR | 4 skipped, no failures |
| `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=4,5,6 python3 -m pytest -v test/manual/kv_transfer/test_disaggregation_staging_nixl_xpu.py` | this PR + #43299 | 4/4 passed, 94 s |
| same, `-k concurrent` | this PR + #43299 | 6 of 6 runs passed |
| same, `-k concurrent` | this PR without the NIXL fix commit, + #43299 | Failed in 4 of 6 runs: the shortest prompt returned one of two fixed wrong continuations. With `SGLANG_DISAGG_STAGING_BUFFER` unset it passed 3 of 3 |
| `test_nixl_backend_basic.py`, `test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`, `test_nixl_dsv4_kv_slots.py`, `test_nixl_sender_failure_cleanup.py` (CPU) | this PR | 63 passed |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No CUDA-path performance regression is intended. The changes are mostly device selection and stream/event handling, on initialization or correctness-critical paths.
- The staging gather resolves the current stream per call instead of holding a fixed stream. The per-call lookup is intentional: the current stream is thread-local, and transfer workers run on separate threads.
- On XPU, the NIXL fix waits on each decode rank's staging write before the next rank's gather, so with decode TP above prefill TP, one request's per-rank writes no longer overlap the next rank's gather. That overlap was what corrupted KV. Mooncake already writes the staging buffer synchronously, and other devices are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
